site.title: Kumotori Hut
site.tagline: A mountain hut at Kumotori Saddle, 2,017 m, open late June to October.

categories.name: Trail notes
categories.description: Conditions on the three routes, week by week.

categories.description: The stove, the kitchen and the people who keep the hut.

categories.name: Season
categories.description: Opening, closing and the weather in between.

posts.title: The zigzag is clear
posts.excerpt: The last snow patch on the Mizuhara zigzag melted this week; light crampons can stay at home.
posts.content:
The north-facing zigzag above Futamata kept its snow until the second week of the season this year. It is now clear all the way to the saddle.

Carry a shell anyway. The wind on the last two hundred metres is the same as ever.

posts.title: Larches on the ridge
posts.excerpt: The larches below the Okuyama ridge are turning; the best week is usually the second in October.
posts.content:
Every year the larches turn from the top down. This morning the highest trees were already gold, and the lower slope still green.

If you can choose one weekend for the ridge route, choose the middle of October and start early.

posts.title: What we cook at 2,017 metres
posts.excerpt: Rice, miso soup with wild greens and a stew that has been on the stove since noon.
posts.content:
Everything for the kitchen comes up by helicopter twice a season, or on our backs. So dinner is simple: rice, miso soup, pickles and a stew.

Breakfast is at 5:30 so that walkers on the ridge can be off before the wind gets up.

posts.title: The spring below the hut
posts.excerpt: Two hundred metres down a stone path is the spring that has never run dry.
posts.content:
The hut takes its water from a spring a short walk below the saddle. In the driest August we have known it still filled a bucket in two minutes.

Please boil it, or use the hot water from the stove.

posts.title: A clear night in September
posts.excerpt: When the cloud sits in the valley, the saddle stands above it under the stars.
posts.content:
On a few nights each September the cloud fills the valley and the hut stands on an island. Lights in the bunk room go out at 20:30; the terrace stays open.

Bring a warm layer. It is close to freezing by midnight.
